editorial:
Imagine an election night broadcast where the hosts have completely lost their minds and don't care about the rules anymore. You get Iain Lee and Katherine Boyle leading a chaotic show that feels more like a late-night party than a news report. The whole vibe is wild and unpredictable, focusing on the absurdity of politics rather than the actual boring numbers. It is essentially the version of a political special that would normally get a station shut down for being too edgy and out of control.

What really works here is the chemistry between the two leads, as they bounce off each other with great energy. The pacing is fast, and the jokes hit hard because they feel spontaneous. While it might be a bit too loud for some, it is a breath of fresh air if you are tired of stiff news anchors. You should definitely check this out if you love awkward humor. Since it is a smaller production, streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video is your best bet for a crisp picture, or you can just rent it on Apple TV for a quick laugh tonight.
endingExplained: The show wraps up by leaning fully into the madness of the election night. Instead of a polished conclusion, the hosts basically crash the party and mock the seriousness of the political process. They end on a high note of irony, showing that the real joke is the system itself. It does not have a traditional plot twist, but it concludes with the feeling that the hosts have successfully broken every rule in the broadcasting book.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves satirical comedy and hates boring news.
